issues.quote: Instagram is acquired, and the new owner runs its own CDN. This really happened. Instagram most probably used Cloudflare as its CDN;
issues.problem: "This really happened." puts a flat assertion of fact directly in front of the teacher's hedged claim ("most probably"). The hedged claim is also the one the fact-check marks wrong: it was CloudFront, not Cloudflare. A reader takes the certainty as covering the Cloudflare story. The SourceNote corrects it, but the page still overstates the teacher's confidence.
issues.evidence: transcript 01:06:42 'Imagine Instagram. Most probably Cloudflare as a CDN. Most probably they were using Cloudflare'; L-0127 detail 'Teacher hedges ("most probably")'; factcheck L-0127 wrong/low (SN-03).
issues.fix: Replace the first three sentences with: "Instagram is acquired by Facebook, which runs its own CDN. In the lecture's telling, Instagram most probably used Cloudflare as its CDN; after Facebook acquired it, it could no longer use that CDN and had to move to Facebook's." [[L-0127]] (Keep SN-03 directly after the paragraph.)

issues.quote: expiry, sig = url.params["oe"], url.params["oh"] ... return error("bad URL")            # someone edited the URL ... return error("Bad URL timestamp")  # the URL has expired
issues.problem: The code drops the teacher's hedge and states as fact that oe is the expiry and oh the signature. The prose two paragraphs earlier keeps the hedge. The code also invents a mapping between two error messages: a failed signature gives "bad URL", an expired URL gives "Bad URL timestamp". The class saw only one message, "Bad URL timestamp", and only after some parameters were removed, not after the URL expired.
issues.evidence: transcript 01:24:48 'OE, this is most probably the expiry. I don't know what this internal parameters are. It's very specific to Facebook CDN' (L-0170, unverifiable); L-0171 'removing some of these query parameters made the request fail with "Bad URL timestamp"'; L-0178 'otherwise it returns bad URL'.
issues.fix: Make the first comment line `# illustrative: oe is most probably the expiry, oh the hash (a guess; Facebook's CDN doesn't document them)` and use one error for both checks: `return error("bad URL")  # L-0178`. Drop the "Bad URL timestamp" mapping, or comment it as `# the demo's message when parameters were removed (L-0171)`. [[L-0170 L-0171 L-0178]]
